mutants.description: sync_out samples async_in directly, bypassing meta_ff: a one-stage synchroniser with one clock less latency
mutants.reason: Every edge on async_in reaches sync_out one clock earlier than the two-flop design (latency 1 instead of 2); also meta_ff becomes unused in the data path, so after reset sync_out tracks async_in from the first clock rather than showing RESET_VALUE for two clocks.

mutants.description: sync_out resets to a hard-coded 0 instead of RESET_VALUE; only meta_ff honours the parameter
mutants.reason: For the RESET_VALUE=1 instances (CP/OTP/UVLO/latch_stat/CS_n), sync_out reads 0 (fault not asserted / CS_n active) during reset and the first clock after release, instead of the safe value 1.

mutants.description: meta_ff resets to a hard-coded 0 instead of RESET_VALUE, so the first stage forgets the safe value
mutants.reason: For RESET_VALUE=1 instances, on the first clock after reset release sync_out drops to 0 (fault de-asserted / CS_n low) for one clock before the real async_in level arrives, regardless of the input.

mutants.description: meta_ff resets to the opposite of RESET_VALUE (safe level misremembered for the first stage)
mutants.reason: For every instance, on the first clock after reset release sync_out shows the inverse of RESET_VALUE for one clock (e.g. Osc/SCK sync pulse high, CS_n sync goes low) before async_in propagates.
